issues.subcategory: Contradictory timing of interventions
issues.description: The introduction explicitly states that interventions will be placed BEFORE the collaborative recall phase, but the Methods/Procedure section clearly places them AFTER collaborative recall (Phase 3 follows Phase 2). This is a fundamental contradiction about the experimental design that makes it impossible to evaluate the study's logic, as the theoretical rationale differs depending on timing (inoculation before exposure vs. post-warning after exposure).
issues.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation).

issues.subcategory: Contradictory test format (open-ended vs. forced-choice)
issues.description: The Procedure section states the individual memory test will use 20 open-ended questions, and the analysis plan initially describes four indices derived from open-ended responses (correct, misinformation-consistent, other, total). However, later in the Analysis Plan, the authors state the test will 'also use the two-alternative forced-choice format,' which contradicts the open-ended description. It is unclear which format will actually be used, making the scoring system and analysis plan uninterpretable.
issues.quote: In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.subcategory: Counterbalancing claim contradicted by fixed items
issues.description: The Design section states that 'discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced,' but the Procedure section states that 'each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.' If all pairs discuss the same four items, there is no counterbalancing—discussed vs. non-discussed status is completely confounded with item content. Any difference between discussed and non-discussed items could reflect item difficulty rather than misinformation effects.
issues.quote: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric's cap color and his company logo.

issues.subcategory: Non-independence of paired data
issues.description: Pairs of participants are the unit of randomization to conditions, and the misinformation each participant receives comes from their partner. This creates non-independence within pairs: one member's responses during collaborative recall directly determine the misinformation the other receives. However, the analysis plan treats individuals as the unit of analysis (ANOVA on individual scores) without accounting for the nested/paired structure. This violates the independence assumption of ANOVA and can inflate Type I error rates.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups... The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA

issues.subcategory: No MORI manipulation check
issues.description: There is no mention of checking whether participants could only see their designated movie version through the polarized glasses, or whether any participant detected they were watching different movies. MORI studies typically include manipulation checks (e.g., asking participants whether they noticed anything unusual about the movie) and exclude participants who detected the manipulation. The only exclusion criterion mentioned is 'technical problems.'
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.subcategory: Interventions not matched for format, duration, or engagement
issues.description: The three interventions differ substantially in modality and engagement level. Extended Warning and Education about Memory are passive ~7-minute podcasts, while Demonstration and Motivation involves an interactive DRM task with personalized feedback plus a podcast. Differences in outcomes could reflect differences in engagement, duration, interactivity, or personal relevance rather than the specific content of each intervention. Without equating these features, the between-group comparison is confounded.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used

issues.subcategory: No experimenter blinding
issues.description: There is no mention of experimenter blinding to condition. The experimenter administers the DRM task in the Demonstration and Motivation condition and presumably plays different podcasts for different groups. If the same experimenter also administers the individual memory test, demand characteristics and experimenter expectancy effects could bias results.

issues.subcategory: Meta-analytic effect size based on only two highly discrepant studies
issues.description: The joint effect size (g = 1.13) for the memory conformity effect is derived from only two studies with wildly discrepant results (g = 1.92 vs. g = 0.38—a 5-fold difference). A random-effects meta-analysis with k = 2 produces an extremely imprecise estimate with an unreliable between-study variance component (tau²). The resulting power analysis is therefore built on a highly uncertain foundation. The I² would likely be very high, suggesting the combined estimate is not meaningfully interpretable.
issues.quote: The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges' g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges' g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020).

issues.subcategory: Demonstration and Motivation confounds multiple active ingredients
issues.description: The Demonstration and Motivation condition contains two distinct active components: (1) demonstrating memory fallibility via DRM, and (2) motivating resistance via a podcast about courtroom consequences. If this condition is effective, it is impossible to determine which component (or their interaction) drove the effect. This limits the theoretical interpretability of results.
issues.quote: The third method of reducing suggestive influence in the context of memory conformity is called Demonstration and motivation. In essence, it consists of two elements: (1) directly demonstrating the fallibility of memory to the participants, and (2) motivating them to provide correct answers

issues.subcategory: Ruling out normative influence without justification
issues.description: The authors assert that normative influence is 'completely ruled out' because the memory test is individual. However, normative influence during the collaborative recall phase could still affect encoding of misinformation (e.g., publicly agreeing with a partner to avoid conflict may strengthen the misinformation trace). The residual effects of normative pressure during discussion could carry over to the individual test. This assumption is too strong and unwarranted.
issues.quote: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing.

issues.subcategory: No primary outcome specified
issues.description: The analysis plan mentions four indices from the open-ended test (correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, total answers), plus accuracy on filler/non-discussed/discussed questions, but does not specify which is the primary outcome. This creates undisclosed researcher degrees of freedom and makes it unclear how to evaluate the study's success or failure.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test's scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers.

issues.subcategory: No plan for handling disagreements during collaborative recall
issues.description: The procedure states that if participants cannot agree during collaborative recall, both responses will be documented. However, there is no analysis plan for how these cases will be treated. Will the item still be coded as 'discussed' and 'containing misinformation'? This is important because partial or no agreement may mean misinformation was not effectively delivered.
issues.quote: If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented.

issues.subcategory: Active control condition may confound comparisons
issues.description: The control group listens to a podcast about soft skills related to social attitudes. This is not an inert control—it could prime social awareness, cooperation, or interpersonal sensitivity, which could either increase or decrease susceptibility to social misinformation. A truly inert filler task (e.g., an unrelated cognitive task) would provide a cleaner baseline.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.subcategory: No plan to verify misinformation delivery
issues.description: Although the collaborative recall discussions will be audio recorded, there is no stated plan to code or analyze these recordings to verify that misinformation was actually exchanged. If partners happened to agree (e.g., through guessing), no misinformation would be delivered for that item. Without verification, the within-subjects comparison is weakened.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded.

issues.subcategory: No correction for multiple comparisons specified
issues.description: The analysis plan states that follow-up pairwise comparisons between groups will be performed if the omnibus interaction is significant, and that 'Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.' However, no correction for multiple comparisons (e.g., Bonferroni, Tukey HSD) is specified. With 6 pairwise comparisons and directional tests, uncorrected alpha inflation is substantial.
issues.quote: In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

issues.subcategory: No plan for ANOVA assumption checking
issues.description: The analysis plan specifies repeated-measures ANOVA but provides no plan for checking assumptions (normality, sphericity, homogeneity of variance) or what remedial actions will be taken if assumptions are violated (e.g., Greenhouse-Geisser correction, non-parametric alternatives, robust methods).
issues.quote: The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels

issues.subcategory: No plan for handling missing data or attrition
issues.description: There is no discussion of how missing data will be handled (e.g., listwise deletion, imputation), what attrition rate is expected, or what will happen if participants drop out after being paired (rendering their partner's data potentially unusable). Given that the unit of randomization is the pair, losing one member of a pair has implications for the other.

issues.subcategory: Insufficient detail on randomization procedure
issues.description: The manuscript states that pairs will be 'randomly assigned' to conditions but provides no details about the randomization method (e.g., simple randomization, block randomization, stratification). With only 30 pairs per group, imbalances in participant characteristics are plausible without stratification.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups

issues.subcategory: DRM demonstration administered to pairs jointly
issues.description: In the Demonstration and Motivation condition, the DRM procedure appears to be administered to both members of a pair simultaneously (the experimenter reads lists aloud). This means participants may observe each other's recall performance, introducing additional social dynamics (e.g., embarrassment, social comparison) that are unique to this condition and could confound interpretation.
issues.quote: it will consist of the participants listening to experimenter presenting lists of words from a common category

issues.subcategory: Restricted age range limits generalizability
issues.description: Participants are restricted to ages 16–35. While the rationale for avoiding large age gaps within pairs is reasonable, the authors do not acknowledge that findings may not generalize to older adults, who represent a substantial portion of real-world eyewitnesses and may differ in memory conformity susceptibility.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.subcategory: No ethical approval or minor consent details
issues.description: The age range includes minors (16–17 years old), but there is no mention of ethical approval, informed consent procedures, or parental/guardian consent for minor participants. This is a significant reporting gap for a study involving human subjects, especially minors.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old

issues.subcategory: Conflicting theoretical predictions for interventions
issues.description: The authors acknowledge that both Education about Memory and Demonstration and Motivation could theoretically increase suggestibility (by reducing confidence in one's own memory), yet they still predict these methods will reduce memory conformity. The theoretical framework does not provide a clear mechanism to predict which direction the effect will go, making the hypotheses somewhat unfalsifiable—any direction of result could be explained post hoc.
issues.quote: presenting participants with research confirming the fallibility of memory may result in decreased confidence in their own memory, which, in turn, might result in increased suggestibility... Of course, demonstrating memory fallibility alone could have different results: it could even increase suggestibility

issues.subcategory: DRM false memory as demonstration of social misinformation vulnerability
issues.description: The DRM paradigm demonstrates vulnerability to associative/semantic memory errors, not vulnerability to social misinformation from co-witnesses. These are fundamentally different memory phenomena involving different mechanisms. Participants may not perceive the DRM demonstration as relevant to their susceptibility to interpersonal influence, potentially undermining the theoretical basis of the Demonstration and Motivation intervention.
issues.quote: The demonstration of the fallibility of memory will be done by means of the DRM technique... Demonstrating the individual fallibility of memory should make the participants alert to the real possibility that their reports may be distorted as a result of a discussion with the partner.

issues.subcategory: Exploratory analyses insufficiently constrained
issues.description: The plan mentions exploratory analyses (DRM as predictor of MORI performance, hypothesis awareness analysis) without specifying the statistical approach, covariates, or how results will be interpreted relative to confirmatory analyses. This leaves substantial room for post-hoc analytic decisions.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.subcategory: Suspiciously low within-subjects correlation
issues.description: The correlation of r = 0.07 between discussed and non-discussed items used in the power analysis is unusually low for repeated measures on the same participants. This value critically affects power calculations for both within-subjects and interaction effects. If the true correlation is higher (as is typical in memory studies), the actual power for the within-subjects effect would be higher but the required N for the interaction could change. The basis for this estimate (only two prior studies) is fragile.
issues.quote: The joint correlation of results in the discussed and non-discussed items in both studies available was 0.07.

issues.subcategory: Certainty ratings collected but no analysis plan specified
issues.description: The procedure describes collecting subjective certainty ratings (0–100%) for each answer, but the analysis plan contains no mention of how these data will be analyzed. Given that confidence-accuracy relationships are theoretically important in eyewitness memory research, the absence of an analysis plan for these data is a notable gap.
issues.quote: for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% (complete uncertainty, guessing) to 100% (absolute certainty)

issues.subcategory: Extended Warning includes enlightenment unique to that condition
issues.description: The Extended Warning condition includes an 'enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception' (revealing that partners saw different movies). This is a fundamentally different type of information than what the other conditions receive—it directly reveals the experimental manipulation. If this condition is effective, it could be entirely due to the enlightenment component rather than the warning or education elements, confounding interpretation.
issues.quote: an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception

issues.subcategory: No detail on how open-ended responses will be scored
issues.description: The individual memory test uses open-ended questions, but there is no description of the scoring rubric, who will score responses, whether inter-rater reliability will be assessed, or how ambiguous responses will be categorized into the four indices (correct, misinformation-consistent, other, no answer).
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation), and (4) the overall number of answers.
